title: What If Every Coral Reef on Earth Died?

scenes.text: What if all coral reefs died? They cover a tenth of one percent of the sea floor.
Yet up to a quarter of all marine creatures rely on them to survive.
About five hundred million people depend on reefs for food, income and protection.
Reefs also act as natural breakwaters, so coastlines would take more of every storm's force.
Tourism, fishing and shoreline protection add up to about thirty billion dollars a year, by one estimate.
A tenth of a percent of the sea floor, holding up a quarter of ocean life. Lose it, and the whole ocean notices.
